Friday ✅. Look out below! 😬

Today's newsletter is 590 words, a 2-minute read.

📉 The dashboard: The S&P 500 closed down 3.7%.

🥶 Today's stock spotlight: Nvidia (-14.0%) See below 👇
 
 
1 big thing: Bloodbath
 
Data: Financial Modeling Prep; Chart: Pete Gannon/Axios

Well, that party didn't last long.

  • Nvidia shares plunged 14% and Anthropic shares surrendered most of their IPO gains today amid a brutal tech stock rout, as the AI boom veered closer to bust.

Why it matters: Anthropic's record IPO has failed to save the flagging AI trade from the weight of declining confidence, tightening credit and a scandal at the world's most important chipmaker.

  • The tech-heavy Nasdaq plunged 5.3% today.

‼️ Stunning stat: Nvidia — which operates at the center of the AI economy as a critical chips supplier, investor and cheerleader — has now lost more than $2.5 trillion in market cap from its all-time high on Oct. 6.

  • The company is grappling with the fallout from the Jensen Huang scandal, plus fears that AI spending isn't sustainable.
  • Today, Reuters reported that the SEC is investigating Nvidia's accounting practices.

Anthropic shares tumbled 8.5% in their first full day of trading after Thursday's biggest-ever IPO.

  • At $88.91, the stock sits just above its IPO price of $83 and far below its first-day high of $115.10, reached shortly after trading opened midday yesterday.

🗣️ What they're saying: "Right now the market is selling first and asking questions later," writes Michael Monaghan, partner at Founder ETFs.

The bottom line: "'Anthropic's blockbuster IPO, which priced at a record valuation, quickly turned into a sentiment inflection point as shares slid sharply from the open, dragging the broader AI ecosystem lower," writes Mark Hackett, chief market strategist at Nationwide.

2. A tremendous tax
 

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios
 

President Trump today said he would block U.S. companies from building data centers overseas or impose a "tremendous tax" on them if they do, Axios' Julianna Bragg writes.

Reality check: It's unclear how Trump would implement the proposed tax, since Congress has the constitutional authority to impose federal taxes.

  • Trump did not specify whether he would seek congressional approval or use existing executive powers to penalize companies that attempt to build data centers outside the U.S.

By the numbers: As of December 2025, 4,000 data centers were operational, with almost 3,000 under construction or planned across the U.S.

4. 🕔 After hours: Kevin!
 

Macaulay Culkin walks the red carpet during the 78th Emmy Awards in Los Angeles on Sept. 14. Photo: Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images
 

If you're thirsty for more "Home Alone," you've waited long enough.

  • Macaulay Culkin is working with Disney's 20th Century Studios to develop a "Home Alone" sequel, Deadline reports.

🍿 State of play: This comes after Culkin recently floated an idea for a new film in the franchise in which his Kevin McCallister would be a dad locked out of the house by his son, who's setting traps for him.

  • Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg are reportedly writing and producing the project in partnership with Culkin, according to Deadline.
  • It's unclear whether they're going with Culkin's original idea or something else.

💭 Nathan's thought bubble: Listen, might it be terrible? Yes. Will I be first in line to see it? Also yes. Bring on the nostalgia.
